messages:
ajay: Quick RFC follow-up — we need a concrete plan for sampling + cost-attribution boundaries for the observability pipelines. Proposal: separate billing events from high-cardinality trace/span attrs, emit a lightweight cost stream for aggregation.

sasha: +1. can you sketch the shape? worried about propagation of sampling decisions across async services (queues, webhooks).

ajay: sketch below. key ideas: 1) runtime emits full span as today; 2) runtime also emits a compact `billing_event` to the cost-topic for every request we care about (sampled or flagged); 3) `billing_event` contains hashed/bucketed id fields to keep cardinality low. sampling_decision_id is attached to spans so we can correlate when we need to backfill.

ajay: example span attrs (unchanged):
```
span.attributes = {
  "http.method": "POST",
  "model.name": "redwood/gpt-4x",
  "user.id": "user_12345",
  "request.tokens": 312
}
```

ajay: example billing_event (compact):
```
{
  "billing_event_id": "b_ev_1f2d",
  "customer_id_hash": "h_3a9f",
  "model_id_bucket": "gpt-4x:bucket-16",
  "tokens_bucket": "256-512",
  "sampling_decision_id": "sd_99",
  "timestamp": 1778880001
}
```

mike: tail-sampling + correlation across async queues is a pain. we should: always keep 100% sampling for errors & latency outliers, probabilistic for normal requests, and allow deterministic sampling by customer id (for debugging paid customers).

sasha: how do we keep billing accuracy? finance needs per-token numbers for invoices. if billing_event buckets tokens we lose precision.

karla: finance note — we need accurate per-customer token counts for invoicing; approximate is fine for internal dashboards but invoiceable numbers must be within 1% of true. retention for raw events for audits: 90 days cold, aggregated 2y.

ajay: plan: two streams. (A) cost-precise stream: emitted only for invoice-eligible events (deterministically sampled by customer plan) with exact token counts, goes to KMS-encrypted topic and retained 90 days; (B) aggregated-cost stream: bucketed events for high-volume customers and telemetry (used for unit economics, alerts). That keeps storage costs down while meeting Karla's constraint.

mike: implementation detail: add `sampling_decision_id` header to messages so async consumers can attach to billing_event even if the span is sampled out. ensures joinability.

sasha: cardinality controls: we should standardize a small set of billing tags: {customer_tier, model_family, region, rollout_flag}. Persist `model.version` only in precise stream. Use hash+salt for customer_id in aggregated stream.

ajay: agree. also add a config-driven top-k exporter: if a tag grows high-cardinality, we auto-promote top-k values and bucket the rest as `other`. avoids OOMs in prometheus-like systems.

ajay: migration: runtime emits both current trace schema and new billing_event for 4 weeks, consumers switch to cost-topic, then we flip. Backfill via ad-hoc job for last-30d if needed.

karla: required for rollout: schema registry entry for `billing_event.v1`, docs for auditors, and an e2e test proving invoice parity within 1%.

mike: I'll prototype sampling lib and sd propagation. sasha can you own schema + top-k exporter? ajay will coordinate runtime changes. karla owns finance acceptance criteria.

sasha: assigned. I'll open a small RFC addendum with the schema and a migration checklist.

deploy-bot: schema-registry: `billing_event.v1` created by sasha at 1778880400 — follow-up: please register compatible changes only. :robot_face:

ajay: next steps: sasha RFC addendum by EOD Friday, mike prototype in 2 wks, small e2e invoice parity check before we enable precise stream for all customers. tagging owners here: @sasha @mike @karla :thumbsup:

sasha: noted. will include sample kinesis/consumer config and retention SLOs.

mike: thumbs up. I'll start a spike to measure extra QPS on cost-topic and put limits on burst.

karla: fine by me. please cc finance on the RFC for billing edge-cases.

ajay: awesome. closing this thread, will link RFC addendum once opened.
